files.item: Slavery: The Hidden History 2007 flyer black and white poster
files.notes: Adapted from an engraving in Histoire d'Angleterre Book III by François Anne David (1741–1824), 1800. The engraving depicts Tacky's Revolt, which occurred in Jamaica between 1760–1761. Slavery: A Hidden History was the spring series of events from 2007.

This was the printed programme from Slavery: A Hidden History, the spring series of events from 2007. The front is adapted from a 'gallows ticket' for the execution of Jonathan Wild (1682 or 1683–1725), engraved by Thomas Cook (c.1744–1818). The gallows ticket was also adapted into the BRHG logo, and used for the Bristol Radical History Week 2006 poster.

After the film poster for The Usual Suspects, 1995. The characters are: a witch from Der junge weisse König erhält Unterricht in Schwarzer Magie und verwehrt sich dagegen, Holzschnitt, by Hans Burgkmair (1473–1531), an illustration from a proof for 'Der Weisskunig', 1516; Blackbeard from A General History of the Robberies and Murders of the Most Notorious Pyrates, by Captain Charles Johnson, 1724; a smuggler from English's Reminiscences of Old Folkestone Smugglers and Smuggling Days, by 'an Old Folkstoner', published by John English, original engraving by William Heath (1795–1840); 'The Batman' from Ogden's Cigarette Cards 'Smugglers & Smuggling', 1932; Ann Mills from an engraving by Robert Graves (1798–1873), date unknown.

The printed programme of events for Witches, Pirates & Smugglers, which was the autumn series of events from 2007. The front cover shows: a witch from Der junge weisse König erhält Unterricht in Schwarzer Magie und verwehrt sich dagegen, Holzschnitt, by Hans Burgkmair (1473–1531), an illustration from a proof for 'Der Weisskunig', 1516; Blackbeard from A General History of the Robberies and Murders of the Most Notorious Pyrates, by Captain Charles Johnson, 1724; a smuggler from English's Reminiscences of Old Folkestone Smugglers and Smuggling Days, by 'an Old Folkstoner', published by John English, original engraving by William Heath (1795–1840); 'The Batman' from Ogden's Cigarette Cards 'Smugglers & Smuggling', 1932; Ann Mills from an engraving by Robert Graves (1798–1873), date unknown.

files.item: A flyer for Merry Hell, an event from Witches, Pirates & Smugglers 2007
files.notes: Merry Hell was an evening of films, held has a Halloween event at The Cube. The skeleton musicians are from La grand danse macabre des hommes et des femmes …, 1641 (the original text is from 1499). The camper van refers to the 1975 film Race with the Devil. The dancing skeletons on top of the camper van are from 'Dance of Death' by Michael Wolgemut (1434–1519) in The Nuremberg Chronicle by Hartmann Schedel (1440–1514), 1493, they were also used to the Miscellaneous 2018 event series poster. The two dancing skeletons in the foreground are from Der doten dantz mit figuren, clage vnd antwort schon von allen staten der werlt by Heinrich Knoblochtzer (1445–1500), 1488. Witches, Pirates & Smugglers was the autumn series of events from 2007.

files.item: A flyer for Pirate Day, which was part of Witches, Pirates & Smugglers 2007
files.notes: The map background is from Nicolas Visscher II's (1649–1702) c. 1680 map of the West Indies, Insulae Americanae in Oceano Septentrionali ac regiones adiacentes: a C. de May usque ad Lineam Aequinoctialem.. The cherubs holding banners are from the same map. The pictures of Anne Bonny and Mary Read comes A General History of the Robberies and Murders of the Most Notorious Pyrates, by Captain Charles Johnson, 1724. Witches, Pirates & Smugglers was the autumn series of events from 2007.

files.item: Web-poster for the Miscellaneous 2007 event series.
files.notes: A reworking of the Bristol Radical History Week 2006 Revolutionary Atlantic poster. Adapted from an engraving of Mary Read in Histoire generale des pirates Historia der Engelsche Zee Roovers In het Engelsch beschreeven, 1725, the Dutch translation of Captain Charles Johnson's A general history of the pyrates, from their first rise and settlement in the island of Providence, to the present time …. In the poster, Mary Read is mistakenly captioned as Anne Bonny.
